If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for bearish bias.

If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.49) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.

If sentiment is positive but recent price is declining, add a 0.5–1.0% downward adjustment to forecast for mid horizon to align with momentum reversal.

If sentiment is negative but recent price is rising, add a 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment to forecast for early horizon to counteract sentiment-driven overcorrection.

If sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.49) and forecast deviates >0.8% from true path, apply a 0.2–0.5% correction in direction of true path for late horizon to stabilize convergence.
